comment: Budgets of the latency gate (performance spec, benches/latency_gate.rs) on the reference runner (ho-z10). Targets are configuration: change them here, with a recorded reason, never in code. Every gated value is the median over the gate's rounds of a per-round p99 (or of the throughput). 4MB proxy overhead set to 16 ms: a loaded shared host showed p99 tails near 12 ms at a 4.6 ms median.

engine.comment: Added request latency through the LLM proxy with the production engine (outgoing::prepare, scrim-redact redactor and guard) on the redaction benchmark's 1 MB bodies. The spec's initial targets are 5 ms (1,000 secrets) and 10 ms (10,000); the production guard does not meet them. Measured on ho-z10 (PR #153): p50 24 to 29 ms, p99 31 to 42 ms across 10, 1,000 and 10,000 secrets, with about a third of the samples dropped for run-queue delay because the guard's four worker threads share three CPUs. Budgets are about 1.5 times the highest p99 so the runner's spread does not fail the gate; a larger slowdown fails here, a smaller one fails the regression check. Tighten them as the guard gets faster.

core.comment: The redaction core on its own, as the scrim-redact benchmarks measure it: Snapshot::protect per 1 MB request with the default thread count, and single-thread Redactor::redact throughput (the per-core minimum of the performance spec). Measured on ho-z10 (PR #153): protect p99 21 to 34 ms; redact 1.6 to 2.4 GB/s on one core. Budgets about 1.5 times the p99 and half the throughput, for the same reason as engine.

regression.comment: The regression check against the previous release (scripts/perfgate). Each gated statistic is compared as the median of its rounds. It regresses when worse than the baseline by more than threshold + noise_factor x the larger relative spread (median absolute deviation) of the two runs' rounds, capped at max_allowed, and by more than the unit's floor. Only runs on the same reference conditions (the match fields) are compared.
